raw.query: SELECT experiment, pool, sla_metric, encoder_workers, p99_ms, max_ms, n_requests FROM provenance.v_pool_latency WHERE window_name='steady24h' AND is_current ORDER BY pool, sla_metric, encoder_workers;
raw.observed: steady24h is a single fixed-rate replay (every row has n_requests=88260; only encoder_workers is swept 1->16). p99 encoder_delay falls 1073->417 ms as workers rise (no load-axis knee). v_grid_static_effective holds 1 row (16->8 workers, burst1->burst2). No saturation knee exists for steady traffic; the only knee curves (sweep_point) are on burst1/head2k, and the ~10x gap there comes from comparing vision in img/s (>255 img/s) vs LLM in req/s (~15 req/s), which collapses to ~2-4x once normalized to req/s (each request carries ~2.88 images).
raw.claimed: Saturation knees an order of magnitude apart on steady traffic.
raw.evidence: Backing views contain no steady-traffic load sweep (knees unreachable: steady vision peak 57 img/s < knee >127 img/s; steady LLM mean 1 req/s << knee ~15 req/s), and the only knee data is burst1/head2k with a 10x that is an img/s-vs-req/s unit artifact.
raw.fix: Re-scope to burst1/head2k (not 'steady'), and compare both pools in the same unit (req/s or normalized img/s); the gap is ~2-4x, not an order of magnitude.
